summary: Ross Bolleter is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Western Australia under David Tunley and trained under John Tarrant and Robert Baker Aitken. From circa 1983 to 2023, he served as a Zen Buddhist teacher at the Zen Group of Western Australia.

Rotem Geva works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned an M.A. from The New School (2005–2007) and a Ph.D. from Princeton University (2007–2014), and served as Department Chair at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 2016.

Roy Rappaport was a scholar of religious studies and related fields. He earned his doctorate at Columbia University (~1959–1966), chaired the anthropology department at the University of Michigan (~1965–1997), and served as president of the American Anthropological Association (~1987–1989).

Roy Tzohar is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tel Aviv University and Columbia University (Ph.D. ~2004–2011) under Gary A. Tubb, Sheldon Pollock, and others, later becoming an associate professor at Tel Aviv University.

Roy W. Perrett is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at the University of Canterbury (~1970–1974) and the University of Otago (~1978–1982). He held posts at Massey University (~1990–2002), the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~2002–2007), and the University of Melbourne.

Royal W. Weiler was an Indologist and linguist who completed his B.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown. He taught at Columbia University (~1958–1961) and served as Assistant Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (~1961–1978).

Royall Tyler is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who earned degrees from Harvard and Columbia, completing his doctorate under Donald Keene. He taught at Ohio State, Wisconsin-Madison, Oslo, and Harvard, and headed the Japan Centre at Australian National University.
Royce Wiles is an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at the Australian National University by 2000 and subsequently held an academic post there.

Rozaliya Osipovna Shor was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Vsevolod Miller. She held researcher posts at RANION, GAKhN, and the Institute of Oriental Studies, and professorships at Baku State University, MPIFL, and institutes in Moscow and Leningrad.

Ruben L. F. Habito is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Ateneo de Manila, Sophia University, and the University of Tokyo, and held posts at Sophia, Southern Methodist University, Ryukoku University, and the Maria Kannon Zen Center.

Rudi Paret was a scholar of religious studies and related fields. He studied at the University of Tübingen (~1920–1924) and later held academic posts at the University of Bonn (~1940–1951) and the University of Tübingen (~1951–1968).

Rudolf Carnap was a philosopher who studied at the universities of Jena, Freiburg, Berlin, and Vienna. He held faculty posts at the University of Vienna (1926), Charles University (1931), the University of Chicago (1936–1952), and UCLA (1954).

Rudolf Ernst Wilhelm Meyer was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Heidelberg University (1873) and earned his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1874–1877), where he was supervised by Albrecht Weber and taught by Johannes Schmidt.

Rudolf Fuchs was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin by 1908 under the supervision of Richard Pischel, also studying under Albrecht Weber, Emil Sieg, and Heinrich Zimmer, among others.
Rudolf Geiger studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from circa 1913 to 1919 and held an academic post at the University of Munich from circa 1937 to 1958.

Rudolf Haym was a scholar of philosophy and history. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and Frederick William University Berlin, later holding a post at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1868.

Rudolf Kaschewsky was a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the universities of Cologne and Bonn, later holding posts at the University of Bonn (1974–2004) and Goethe University Frankfurt.
Rudolf Lange was a scholar in Japanology and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo from circa 1874 to 1881 and at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1887 to 1923.

Rudolf Meringer was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Vienna (Ph.D. 1878–1882) and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at the University of Vienna (1885, 1892) and was professor at the University of Graz (1899–1930).

Rudolf Much was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna from circa 1883 to 1887 and subsequently held an academic post there from circa 1895 to 1934.
